name: Gwri

attributes.attribute: Name given to the kidnapped hero Pryderi by his foster father.
He appeared miraculously from the night sky on Beltane.
Called Gwri Wallt Eurin, meaning golden hair.
Restored to his parents and renamed Pryderi.
Appeared in place of a foal in Teyrnon's household.
Childhood name of Pryderi in the first branch of the Mabinogi.
Foster father who raised and named Gwri.
First branch tells the story of the lost and restored child.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gwri was the childhood name of the hero that Welsh tradition calls Pryderi. He was the son of Rhiannon and Pwyll in a story from the Mabinogi. The boy vanished soon after his birth, so Rhiannon was wrongly blamed for the loss. Teyrnon Twrf Liant, an upright lord, found the child and raised him as his own. Teyrnon gave the boy the name Gwri, and the epithet Wallt Euryn, golden hair, sometimes followed it. MacKillop records that the foster father gave the boy the name. When Gwri grew older he was restored to his birth parents. The boy then took the name Pryderi, under which he plays a large role in later Welsh tales.
